en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya Sakacintaniya Chapter 10 I was once a merchant’s son in the city of Benares; I was wealthy and possessed of great riches. Then, seeing the Blessed One, the Teacher, Seated upon a seat at the foot of a tree, I took a handful of flowers, And having scattered them over the Buddha, I made this aspiration: “May I become a Buddha just like you! Through that root of merit, For ninety-one aeons, I never fell into the four states of misery, But always enjoyed happiness. In my final existence, I was born in a wealthy family; I was handsome, pleasing, and fair to behold, With a complexion like gold. At the time of the Parinibbāna of the Great Sage, I was a king named Mahāpati; Having heard that the Buddha had passed away, I went to the place where the relics were. There I saw a stūpa made of sandalwood, Adorned with a parasol and a pinnacle; I had a flower-basket made, And filled it with various kinds of flowers.

I placed it upon the stūpa, And circumambulated it three times; Having performed this act of merit, I passed away from that human life. By the power of that deed, I was reborn in Tāvatiṃsa; There I enjoyed celestial pleasures For twenty thousand years. When the lifespan there had expired, I was reborn in the human world; I became a king, a lord of the earth, Ruling over the four continents. In that state, I gave alms-food To the Saṅgha of monks led by the Buddha; Having given that gift of food, I passed away from that human life. “Like a fearless lion,
like the king of birds, the garuḍa;
like a noble tiger or a bull— ”
Like a noble lion,
the crested one, refuge of the three worlds,
unshakable and unconquered.
Having placed [the bowl] upon a stand, [he approached] the foremost of ascetics, who was seated and honored by the community of monks.
I scattered the supreme anojā flower,
together with its very calyx,
over the Best of Buddhas.
Through that clarity of mind,
O Indara among bipeds, O Bull among men,
I have attained the unshakable state.
Having abandoned victory and defeat,
that deed which I performed back in the thirty-first aeon from now—
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
In a full thirty kappas,
Named Devabhūti and Sana,
they were five universal monarchs endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya.
The seventh chapter, the Chapter on Sakacintaniya, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
Sakacintī, Avopupphī,
and Sapaccāgamana.
Parappasādī, Bhisada,
Sucinti, Vatthadāyaka,
and Ambadāyī Sumana.
And also the Pupphacaṅkoṭakī;
seventy-one verses have been spoken,
as counted by those who see the meaning.
